extracted.intended_audience: employers, workers, safety professionals, labor advocates, and other stakeholders participating in OSHA rulemaking and public comment on the Heat Injury and Illness Prevention proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Information and procedural guidance for stakeholders on the OSHA proposed Heat Injury and Illness Prevention standard, including scope, deadlines, hearing procedures, and supporting materials for filing comments or participating in the rulemaking. Useful for preparing comments, testimony, or employer compliance planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the proposed standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed standard would apply to all employers conducting outdoor and indoor work in all general industry, construction, maritime, and agriculture sectors where OSHA has jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which employers and sectors are covered by the NPRM and therefore who must comply if the rule is finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer requirement to create a heat-hazard plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard would require employers to create a plan to evaluate and control heat hazards in their workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM is intended to clarify employer obligations and the steps necessary to effectively protect employees from hazardous heat; employers should expect to develop written procedures/plans addressing evaluation and control measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose/goal of the rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate goal is to prevent and reduce the number of occupational injuries, illnesses, and fatalities caused by exposure to hazardous heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this protective purpose as the central justification for proposed measures and for framing comments or compliance strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of heat hazards and affected conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive heat in the workplace can cause a number of adverse health effects, including heat stroke and even death, if not treated properly. Workers in outdoor and indoor work settings without adequate climate controls are at risk of hazardous heat exposure. Certain heat-generating processes, machinery, and equipment (e.g., hot tar ovens, furnaces, etc.) can also cause hazardous heat when cooling measures are not in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background information to support why a federal standard is necessary; can be cited in comments or evidence submissions to demonstrate risk and affected operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how the NPRM was published and accessed
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA's Heat Injury and Illness Prevention in Outdoor and Indoor Work Settings proposed rule was published in the Federal Register on August 30, 2024, and is available for viewing at https://federalregister.gov/d/2024-14824 and at www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should consult the Federal Register notice and the regulations.gov docket for the official text, supporting materials, and how to file comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period for the NPRM (initial comment deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The public comment period for the NPRM closed on January 14, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the deadline for initial public submissions; check Federal Register notices for any extensions or additional comment opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal public hearing and transcript availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The informal public hearing was held June 16 through July 2, 2025. Official hearing transcripts and archived recordings are available (linked on the page) and a compilation of questions OSHA asked of witnesses and a list of common questions are available for reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing transcripts and recordings provide evidence, witness testimony, and questions that may inform post‑hearing comments or briefs; use them to cite testimony or to identify issues raised during the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-hearing comment procedures for NOITA filers
rubrics_metrics.description: The post-hearing comment period for individuals who submitted a Notice of Intention to Appear (NOITA) to file additional evidence and data relevant to the proceeding, as well as final written briefs, ended on October 30, 2025. Post-hearing comments are available for viewing at https://www.regulations.gov/document/OSHA-2021-0009-25504/comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only individuals who filed a NOITA at the informal public hearing were eligible for this post-hearing submission period; reviewers should file NOITAs when required and consult the cited regulations.gov docket to view post-hearing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where public comments and hearing materials are posted
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments received are available for viewing at https://www.regulations.gov/document/OSHA-2021-0009-4761/comment and post-hearing comments at the docket link above; official hearing transcripts are available at https://www.regulations.gov/document/OSHA-2021-0009-25560.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the regulations.gov docket numbers provided to locate and review submitted comments, transcripts, and other record materials when preparing responses or further submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of available supporting documents and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA provides supporting materials including: Heat NPRM Fact Sheet (and Español), NPRM Compilation of Requests for Comment, Recorded OSHA Presentation on the NPRM (and Español), OSHA Presentation Slides on the NPRM (and Español), Background, Previous Actions, Heat Injury and Illness SBREFA, OSHA's Heat Safety and Health Topics Page, OSHA's Heat Illness Prevention Campaign, and the Heat Injury and Illness Prevention Work Group of the National Advisory Committee on Occupational Safety and Health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These materials supply context, data requests, outreach resources, and regulatory history useful for drafting informed comments, preparing testimony, or designing employer compliance programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of extensions and procedural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The docket includes Federal Register Notices such as 'Extension of post-hearing comment period' and 'Extension of comment period and notice of informal hearing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch Federal Register notices for changes to deadlines or hearing arrangements; extensions alter timelines and who may submit certain materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to learn more about OSHA's rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information on OSHA's rulemaking process and how stakeholders can participate is available at https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/rulemakingprocess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders unfamiliar with the federal rulemaking process should consult OSHA's rulemaking process page to understand procedures (NPRM, comments, hearings, post-hearing submissions, dockets) and compliance steps.
